newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Quinn says Ireland will continue to meet EMU needs.
newsitem.headline: Quinn says Ireland will continue to meet EMU needs.

text.p: Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), which will provide for the single currency, will commence on the first of January 1999, Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said in a budget speech on Wednesday.
He said Ireland intends to continue to meet the conditions of EMU entry.

"This means that we must make provision in our future budgetary planning to maintain sufficient headroom to deal with the impact of economic shocks without exceeding the three percent ceiling on the deficit," Quinn said.
Quinn said there is uncertainty regarding the level of EU structural and cohesion funding after the EU's current plan for Ireland expires in 1999.
"The government will, in the forthcoming negotiations, argue that Ireland needs continuing substantial support," the minister said.

We will point to our recent economic progress as evidence of our effective use of EU funds. However, it is only prudent to recognise that there is no assurance that EU funding will continue indefinitely at present rates.

"Because of factors such as these, the government have adopted a strategy that will keep Ireland's General Government Deficit at no more that half of the three percent Maastricht ceiling by 1999, Quinn said.
